newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks pare gains late on weak exports.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks pare gains late on weak exports.

text.p: Singapore stocks retreated late on Monday on heavy selling after disappointment over Singapore's March trade figures, dealers said.
March non-oil exports fell 2.1 percent year-on-year, smaller than expected after last month's fall of 7.9 percent, but still bad enough to cast a cloud over the market.
"Institutions were nibbling, but that's all they were doing. Without good economic foundations in place, demand will continue to be poor," said a dealer with a U.S. investment house.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended down 5.31 points at 2,037.89, well below an intraday high of 2,058.26.
Advancing issues outpaced decliners by 234 to 112 on a moderate turnover of 183 million shares.
The UOB OTC index rose 14.57 points to 1,189.25, supported by more punting interest and a sharp rise in the Kuala Lumpur share index, which closed 2.08 percent higher on the day.
In Singapore, SIA foreign drew interest but gains were pared after profit taking. The stock ended unchanged at $12.00, off from an intraday high of $12.20.
DBS Land also eased off highs at S$4.94 to end at SS4.86, while Keppel Corp fell 25 cents to S$8.70.
